question.text: In the context of AIF fund due diligence, reviewing the manager's significant change in fund size relative to previous funds and ability to invest at the targeted size helps assess:

answer.text: How much office space the fund needs
The personal wealth of the fund manager
The fund manager's ability to attract investor commitments and deploy capital at the targeted scale
The number of employees in the fund house

explanation.text: The Logic: The workbook directs distributors to examine capital commitments raised, any significant change in fund size compared with previous funds, and whether the manager can invest at the targeted size, including the impact of co-investing. These indicators speak to the manager's ability to attract commitments and credibly deploy at the proposed scale. The Trap: Office space, personal wealth, and headcount are not part of the workbook's fund-size or capacity-related due-diligence prompts. Note: Stem and options were rewritten to use the workbook-backed framing (significant fund-size change, ability to invest at targeted size, co-investing impact) instead of an indirect "AUM growth shows investor confidence" claim. Unsupported strategy-drift/capacity threshold guidance was removed.
